GitHub Repos.Why trending: Second-biggest weekly gain among AI repos not featured this fortnight.
GitHub Repos.Why use it: Make an AI coding assistant plan before it codes and work in small, tested steps, so it can run for hours with less supervision.

The skills then trigger on their own. Needs that tool's sign-in; the README also describes optional telemetry for its visual companion, so read it first.

GitHub Repos.Why trending: Next-largest weekly gain after repos covered this fortnight; some plugins connect to Microsoft 365.
GitHub Repos.Why use it: Give a team a ready-made starting point for role-specific AI help, such as call prep or contract review, that they can customize.

In Cowork, install from claude.com/plugins. Connectors link to your work tools, so check permissions first.

GitHub Repos.How to try it: From your project folder run npx impeccable install (needs Node.js), then run /impeccable init inside your AI coding tool such as Claude Code. The checks run locally with no API key; the assistant itself needs your sign-in.

GitHub Repos.What it does: Skills that give coding agents art direction, reference images and a browser check.

GitHub Repos.Why use it: Have an AI assistant review a screen or a code change for accessibility, readability and polish, and return one ranked list of fixes.
GitHub Repos.How to try it: Run npx skills add jakubkrehel/skills (needs Node.js), or in Claude Code run /plugin marketplace add jakubkrehel/skills then /plugin install interfaces@interfaces. Review any skill before use.

GitHub Repos.Why trending: Still rising; 77,078 stars on Oct 20.

GitHub Repos.Why trending: Covers 26 skills and 19 agents, including checks for getting cited by AI search.
GitHub Repos.Why use it: Audit a website for technical, content and AI-search problems without paying for a separate SEO tool.

Research Papers.Bottom line: A cheap predictor filters what a big model runs, cutting compute.

Research Papers.Bottom line: A training-free method keeps 99.6% of accuracy at about a third of the compute.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Cheaper image-and-text AI.

Research Papers.Title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
Research Papers.Bottom line: A video model that infers what you want next and answers 10.7% better.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Assistants that help unasked.

Research Papers.Title: TAO: Tool-Aware Joint Scheduling for LLM-Based Agentic Serving
Research Papers.Bottom line: Smarter GPU scheduling cuts agent latency up to 26.8%.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Lower cost to run agents.

Research Papers.Title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
Research Papers.Bottom line: An open 8B-parameter video world model you steer turn by turn with text and camera moves.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Open-source rival to Google's Genie 4.

Research Papers.Title: Work Agents: Systems, Capabilities, and Optimization
Research Papers.Bottom line: A survey framing AI work agents as a model plus a runtime harness that delivers checkable results.
Research Papers.Why it matters: A shared vocabulary for judging agents.

Research Papers.Title: OmniShowcase: Omnidirectional Subject-Consistent Video Generation from Multi-View Images
Research Papers.Bottom line: Makes videos of an item from four photos that hold shape through full 360-degree turns.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Product video without a shoot.

Research Papers.Title: Intrinsic Distribution Matching
Research Papers.Bottom line: Improves one-step and few-step AI image generation so images follow the prompt's details more closely.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Cheaper, faster images.

Research Papers.Title: A-RSI: Adaptive Task Refresh for Zero-Data Multimodal Self-Improvement
Research Papers.Bottom line: A model improves itself by refreshing its practice tasks when learning stalls, using answers it can check.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Less human-labelled data.

Research Papers.Title: DynaFlow: Learning Free-Form Multi-Agent Orchestration
Research Papers.Bottom line: One main agent writes small programs that coordinate helper agents, deciding when teamwork is needed.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Adaptive agent teams.

Research Papers.Title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
Research Papers.Bottom line: Many dedicated agent-memory systems score below plain retrieval from raw history.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Memory that rewrites facts can lose evidence; keep the raw record.

Research Papers.Title: Efficient Streaming Audio-Visual Target Speaker Extraction for Real-World Acoustic Scenes
Research Papers.Bottom line: Falcon isolates one speaker's voice using lip video, with 91.9% fewer parameters.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Small enough for phones and headsets.

Research Papers.Title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
Research Papers.Bottom line: A robot model that predicts physical motion without slow video generation; 99.3% on LIBERO.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Results are in simulation, not real robots.

Research Papers.Title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
Research Papers.Bottom line: Trains video AI to reason about space across answer types, gaining 13.41 points on one test.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Models trained for one answer format often fail at others.

Research Papers.Title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
Research Papers.Bottom line: Trains agents by crediting whole turns, with gains over strong baselines.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Long multi-step tasks need better credit for each step.

Research Papers.Title: The Trinity: Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
Research Papers.Bottom line: Agents build practice worlds and evolve their own tooling, up 26 points on unseen tests.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Authors' gain includes per-benchmark preparation, per commenters.

Research Papers.Title: Trajectory2Gym: Decision-Grounded Compositional Interaction Synthesis for Tool-Use Agents
Research Papers.Bottom line: Builds better practice runs for tool-using agents, lifting scores 16.9 to 29.8 points.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Quality of training examples beats raw quantity.

Research Papers.Title: StreamVibe: Proactive Video Agents for Evolving User Intent
Research Papers.Bottom line: A video AI that infers what you want next, not just what you ask.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Points toward assistants that offer help unprompted.

Research Papers.Title: Trial by Trace: Benchmarking AI Agent Harnesses for Reliability and Failure Attribution
Research Papers.Bottom line: In 31.1% of runs the agent finished the task while its harness failed a check.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Success alone can hide unreliable agent software.

Research Papers.Title: Reading, Writing, Sharing, and Interacting with the World through Video
Research Papers.Bottom line: A survey of 600+ works linking video understanding and generation through world models.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Says smooth video is not the same as a consistent world.

Research Papers.Title: UserArena: Benchmarking Interactive User Simulation for Long-Horizon Shopping Agents
Research Papers.Bottom line: A benchmark of 64,729 real shopping sessions for testing simulated shoppers.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Checks simulators against a real A/B test.

Research Papers.Title: HiSTEVE 1.0: Harnessing Human-Interface VLA Agents for Open-World Games
Research Papers.Bottom line: An agent plays Minecraft with only vision, keyboard and mouse, crafting an iron pickaxe from scratch.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Scores 85.0% on MineStudio Bench.

Research Papers.Title: Looking Ahead: Modeling Future Evolution in Autoregressive Video Generation
Research Papers.Bottom line: Trains video generators to predict later chunks, so scenes evolve instead of just continuing.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Needs no extra encoder and leaves generation unchanged.

Research Papers.Title: SpatialScout: Can VLM Agents Actively Explore and Map 3D Scenes?
Research Papers.Bottom line: A benchmark of 80 indoor scenes testing whether vision-language agents can explore and locate objects in 3D.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Tests mapping by acting, not just answering questions.

Research Papers.Title: Deep Search in Real-World Web Environments
Research Papers.Bottom line: OpenDS tests agents on multi-step research across the live, messy web.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Most prior tests used static data.

Research Papers.Title: Spectral-Spatial Interpretation
Research Papers.Bottom line: Explains which image channels matter, and where in the image.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Beats rival methods using about 6% of the compute on one test.

Research Papers.Title: Editing Images into Reusable Layers via Compositional Edit-Prior Distillation
Research Papers.Bottom line: LayerEditor edits an image and returns reusable layers, not one flat picture.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Makes precise local edits easier to reuse.

Research Papers.Title: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
Research Papers.Bottom line: LGWM predicts what the next screen should look like to catch unsafe clicks.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Trained on 1.85M real screen transitions.

Research Papers.Title: WeVisOne-VL: Unified Visual Perception from Objects to Pixels
Research Papers.Bottom line: One open model finds, counts, reads and cuts out objects in images.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Leads on 30+ vision benchmarks, per the authors.

Research Papers.Title: Making MLLM Latents Matter: Factor-Aware Predictive Learning for Cinematic Video Generation
Research Papers.Bottom line: Uses a language model's understanding to steer video generation.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Better control of character, scene and camera.

Research Papers.Title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
Research Papers.Bottom line: Small looped models learn to track much longer sequences than they trained on.
Research Papers.Why it matters: 95.5% accuracy at 16x training length on one test.

Research Papers.Title: StreamEval: Evaluating Interactive Streaming Video Generation Models
Research Papers.Bottom line: First benchmark for AI video that reacts live to requests.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Models look good but follow requests poorly.

Research Papers.Title: EgoXperience: Learning World-Grounded Egocentric Representations from Human Experience
Research Papers.Bottom line: Rebuilds camera, scene, hands and objects in 3D from first-person video.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Cuts camera error by 68.9% versus baselines.

Research Papers.Title: Holi-World: Building Holistic World Intelligence from Human-Ego Experience
Research Papers.Bottom line: Turns first-person recordings into training data for AI that understands scenes.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Cheaper data without manual labelling.

Research Papers.Title: OR-License: Evaluating LLM Agents as Real-World Operations Research Practitioners
Research Papers.Bottom line: Tests whether AI agents can do real planning-and-optimisation work.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Shows how ready agents are for analyst jobs.

Research Papers.Title: Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
Research Papers.Bottom line: Agents that operate screens using several input types.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Better computer-using assistants.

Research Papers.Title: Matrix-Game 4.0: Harnessing Video Models for Real-Time Playable Game Worlds
Research Papers.Bottom line: Uses video models to make game worlds you can play in real time.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Hints at AI-generated interactive worlds.

Research Papers.Title: LEV: Thinking Fast and Deep with Looped Decision Models
Research Papers.Bottom line: Repeats a model's layers to reason deeper without writing tokens.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Better answers on hard questions.

Research Papers.Title: PremiseCheck: Efficient Fact-Checking of Human and AI Peer Reviews
Research Papers.Bottom line: Splits review comments into premises and checks each one.
Research Papers.Why it matters: High accuracy at lower cost.

Research Papers.Title: Scaling Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Brain Encoding
Research Papers.Bottom line: Low-rank adapters tune huge models to predict brain activity.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Cuts compute and aids interpretation.

Research Papers.Title: Has GPT-6-Astra Achieved Embodied Intelligence?
Research Papers.Bottom line: GPT-6-Astra handles robot tasks well, but real deployment is costly and slow.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Competent robots are not yet practical ones.

Research Papers.Title: HexaShell: A Thin Harness for Exploring the Limits of VLM Agents as Robot Coding Agents
Research Papers.Bottom line: A coding agent writes its own tools to drive a two-arm robot: 39.7% success.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Tight-fit tasks still fail (8.3%).

Research Papers.Title: BizBench: Unveiling Hidden Challenges in Deploying Long-Horizon Agents for Real-World Business
Research Papers.Bottom line: On payments tasks, top models fully succeed only about 61-64% of the time.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Rule breaks midway can hide behind final success.

Research Papers.Title: OpenGCUA: Toward a Fully Open Stack for Generalist Computer Use
Research Papers.Bottom line: Open recipe for agents that use a computer, lifting all eight models tested.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Fewer steps per task; closed systems get an open rival.

Research Papers.Title: FDE-Gym: The Last Mile of AI Delivery
Research Papers.Bottom line: Best AI agent fully resolved only 14 of 95 real customer-delivery tasks.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Hidden requirements, not skill, trip agents up.

Research Papers.Title: Agent-Reflex: Teaching Language Agents to Act Reflectively
Research Papers.Bottom line: Trains agents to spot tool errors and recover, scoring 58.6 on five tests.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Real tools fail; sturdier agents waste less.

Research Papers.Title: MJev-Spatial: System One Spatial Intelligence via Native Attention Matching
Research Papers.Bottom line: Answers spatial questions by scoring options directly, with no text generation.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Faster decisions for agents and robots.

Research Papers.Title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
Research Papers.Bottom line: A 4B model that points to objects precisely, ahead of GPT-6 Astra.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Better perception for robots and vehicles.

Research Papers.Title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
Research Papers.Bottom line: A steadier, cheaper way to tune image models with rewards.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Cuts training cost for image and video tools.

Research Papers.Title: OmniCompass: A Holistic Benchmark for Omni-Modal Video Grounding and Understanding
Research Papers.Bottom line: A new test of 820 videos shows AI still struggles to find when and where things happen.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Open models lag proprietary ones on audio plus video.

Research Papers.Title: Waypoint-OPD: Transferring RL-Induced Policy Shifts via Gated On-Policy Distillation
Research Papers.Bottom line: A cheap trick for teaching a small model from a reinforcement-trained one.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Beat other methods in all six math and code tests.

Research Papers.Title: VideoJev: System One Model for Video Understanding and Interaction
Research Papers.Bottom line: Scores answers directly, making video questions up to 100 times faster.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Speed matters for AI agents that watch video.

Research Papers.Title: Any Time, Any Space: A World-State-Centric Framework for Agentic Video Generation
Research Papers.Bottom line: Keeps long AI-made videos consistent using scene and event memory.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Improved consistency across four video generators.

Research Papers.Title: Beyond Domain-Routed Supervision: Cross-Teacher Guarding for Multi-Teacher On-Policy Distillation
Research Papers.Bottom line: Teaches one model from several expert models without them clashing.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Gained over 5 points where teachers conflict most.

Research Papers.Title: Player-1: Learning to Play from Synthetic Experience
Research Papers.Bottom line: Trains AI to play games using practice in made-up environments.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Player-1-9B reached 38.33% on MineDojo-300 versus 12.63% for the best baseline.

Research Papers.Title: Jeva: System One Models from First Principles
Research Papers.Bottom line: A 4-billion-parameter model built for fast picks among options, with a built-in "none of these" answer.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Handles 2,048 candidates and reuse speeds it over 20 times.

Research Papers.Title: Thinking Inertia: LLMs Keep Thinking When Told Not To
Research Papers.Bottom line: Language models keep reasoning visibly even when told to answer only.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Instructions alone can't switch off reasoning, which matters for cost and control.

Research Papers.Title: AgentSWE: Can Coding Agents Build the Agent You Actually Want?
Research Papers.Bottom line: A 25-task test found no coding agent delivers what a requirement asks.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Agents often overfit examples and claim unfinished work is done.

Research Papers.Title: S-Space: Exploring Spatial Workspace in Multimodal Language Models
Research Papers.Bottom line: Explores giving multimodal language models (AI that handles both text and images) a spatial "workspace" for reasoning about where things are.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Spatial reasoning is a known chatbot weak spot; it matters for maps, floor plans, diagrams and robots.

Research Papers.Title: GroundingPI: A Grounding Foundation Model towards Physical Intelligence with Visual Primitives
Research Papers.Bottom line: From EV (electric vehicle) maker XPENG: a model that links language to precise spots in images, aimed at machines acting in the real world.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Grounding (tying words to exact things in a scene) is core to self-driving and robotics.

Research Papers.Title: DiffusionART: Efficient, Stable and Scalable Reinforcement of Diffusion Models
Research Papers.Bottom line: From the team behind the Kling video generator: a more stable, efficient way to improve diffusion models (the tech behind most AI image and video tools).
Research Papers.Why it matters: Cheaper training means faster-improving creative and marketing tools.

Research Papers.Title: RealCompanion: Benchmarking Human Understanding from Reasoning over Longitudinal Real-World Conversations
Research Papers.Bottom line: A new test of whether AI can actually understand a person by reasoning across months of real conversations, not just one chat.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Long-term memory is the new battleground (see Meta's Muse Wonder). This gives the industry a yardstick for whether that memory produces real understanding.

Research Papers.Title: AgentGarten: Code Worlds for Evolving Agents
Research Papers.Bottom line: Builds code-based practice worlds where AI agents can train, try things and improve over time.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Better training environments are exactly what Anthropic says it got wrong this week. Safer, well-designed sandboxes are how agents learn without loose internet access.

Research Papers.Title: Rethinking Cross-Tokenizer On-Policy Distillation: From Alignment Coverage to Supervision Reliability
Research Papers.Bottom line: When teaching a small, cheap AI model to imitate a big one that reads text differently, learning only from the reliably matched parts works better than learning from everything.
Research Papers.Why it matters: Distillation is how powerful AI gets shrunk into fast, affordable models that can run on a laptop or phone. Cheaper models mean wider, more private deployment.

Releases.Name: Strawberry
Releases.Bottom line: A Chromium-based browser (built on the open-source code behind Chrome) with AI 'companions' that do office work inside the accounts you are already signed into, such as sorting email or researching leads. It left beta on October 26. Page content goes to AI providers, so check your workplace rules first.
Releases.Similar to: Perplexity Comet, ChatGPT's Chrome extension, Claude
Releases.Pricing: Free (500 credits a month); paid plans $20, $85 or $250 a month

Releases.Name: Zest concierge
Releases.Bottom line: A restaurant agent you text, with no app to open. It recommends places from your own dining history and your friends', can join a group chat to run a vote, and books tables through OpenTable, Resy and SevenRooms. It uses card data linked through Plaid, restaurant spending only.
Releases.Pricing: Price not published; supported cities not stated

Releases.Name: XREAL AURA
Releases.Bottom line: The first wired glasses running Android XR (Google's operating system for extended reality, meaning digital screens laid over the real world), with Google's Gemini assistant built in. You see the room through clear lenses while apps, movies, games or your laptop screen float in front of you, and you can ask Gemini about whatever you're looking at.
Releases.Similar to: Meta Ray-Ban Display, Apple Vision Pro, Samsung Galaxy XR
Releases.Pricing: From $1,099 (launch price through Dec 2026; normally $1,279); ¥229,800 in Japan. Ships mid-November

Releases.Name: Pebs
Releases.Bottom line: A personal AI agent inside the Nox app: give one of its two characters, Miso or Orbit, an everyday goal and it writes a plan, works through it in its own cloud browser you can watch or take over, and hands back a list, a file or a confirmation. It can repeat tasks on a schedule and asks before it buys, sends or submits anything.
Releases.Similar to: Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots, Grok Bot
Releases.Pricing: Included with Nox MAX ($24.99/mo) and NOX 50 ($49.99/mo); not on Free or Pro

Releases.Name: Kiwi
Releases.Bottom line: A free AI assistant you simply text on iMessage, WhatsApp or SMS, with no app to install. It reads your calendar and email, texts you first when something needs doing (a delayed flight, a bill due, a free Saturday), and books or replies on apps and websites once you say yes, showing the price first.
Releases.Pricing: Free (pilot); you pay merchants directly for anything it books

AI Business.Headline: Solo founder built iPhone privacy app Vaultaire in three weeks with AI coding agents; it reached $41K in a month
AI Business.Revenue: $26,384 gross App Store sales in July, $41,425 in August (self-reported); mostly lifetime purchases, so not recurring
AI Business.Bottom line: Rasty Turek, a former Google engineer who sold his earlier company in 2025, used AI coding agents to build Vaultaire, an iPhone app that hides photos and files behind on-device encryption. He says it went from $66 at launch in March to over $40,000 a month by August.
AI Business.How AI is used: He wrote a product spec, handed it to coding agents, and shipped the first version in about three weeks. AI tools cost about $400 a month; the app has no backend, so hosting is about $5.
AI Business.Lesson: He says almost doubling the price barely changed sales, and that distribution (App Store search, localisation, backlinks) mattered more than the code.

AI Business.Headline: Self-taught filmmaker's one-person AI creative workspace Kolbo.AI reaches about $60K a month
AI Business.Revenue: About $60,000 a month, ten months after launch (self-reported)
AI Business.Bottom line: Zohar Vanunu, a director and 3D artist with no programming background, built Kolbo.AI alone: one workspace with leading AI image, video, audio and chat models, for creators who juggled ten subscriptions. He says there was no outside funding and no paid ads.
AI Business.How AI is used: The product bundles third-party AI models with projects, consistent characters and shared team credits. The source does not say which tools he used to build it.
AI Business.Lesson: He says viral views earned little until he posted a tutorial opening his whole project; signups from abroad jumped 6.5 times that day. Teaching beat pitching.

AI Business.Headline: Ex-Microsoft engineer quits $200K job to build an AI money-coach startup alone, using Claude Code and Codex
AI Business.Revenue: More than $6,000 total revenue so far (self-reported); founder takes no salary
AI Business.Bottom line: Junead Khan, 25, left a Microsoft job that paid over $200,000 to build Treasury, an AI money coach, with no cofounder and no venture capital (outside investor money). It now has paying customers and more than $6,000 in revenue, and he still runs it alone on his savings.
AI Business.How AI is used: He uses the AI coding assistants Claude Code (Anthropic) and Codex (OpenAI) to write software fast enough that he did not need a technical cofounder, and the product itself uses AI to act as a personal finance coach.
AI Business.Lesson: AI coding tools let one person build a real first version, but the hard part is still finding customers, so he built an audience by sharing his journey openly on social media instead of paying for ads.

AI Business.Headline: Solo founder's $1.6M software business now runs on AI agents, cutting costs 61% and his workweek to about 4 hours
AI Business.Revenue: $1,616,235 total revenue through Stripe since October 2021 (self-reported); running costs down from $71K per half-year (late 2024) to $27.5K (first half of 2026)
AI Business.Bottom line: Jordan Rejaud coded his SaaS (software-as-a-service, a subscription app) by hand, and it has taken in over $1.6 million since 2021. Now AI agents run most of the day-to-day work, so he has no employees, works about 4 hours a week, and his costs fell 61%.
AI Business.How AI is used: AI agents (about $117 a month in AI bills) handle customer support, software deploys, server monitoring, email and ads, and they reviewed every expense and replaced paid tools like Auth0, Zendesk and Sentry with open-source or AI-built versions; anything that spends money or messages a person waits for his approval.
AI Business.Lesson: AI does not have to create the business to change it: pointing agents at the boring operations work (support, monitoring, bills) can free your time and cut costs, as long as you keep a human sign-off on money and customer messages.

AI Business.Headline: One founder plus AI agents: Uneed launch platform hits $30K a month
AI Business.Team size: 1 person (plus one partner for directory submissions; first hire coming)
AI Business.Revenue: About $250K over the last 12 months, up about 150%, now about $30K a month (self-reported)
AI Business.Bottom line: Thomas Sanlis runs Uneed, a website where people launch new software products, mostly by himself. It made about $250,000 in the past year, mainly from founders paying $14.99 or $39.99 to skip a free waiting line.
AI Business.How AI is used: He uses Claude to draft support replies he checks each morning, AI to flag low-quality or copycat product listings, and AI coding agents running on a server (which he follows from his phone) to write most of the code and make launch graphics.
AI Business.Lesson: A simple, fair pricing idea (free, but pay to go faster) matters more than the AI; the AI just lets one person handle the volume that idea brings in.
